title: Organic Farming Practices, Compost Enriched Formulations & Bio-stimulants
source: National Centre of Organic and Natural Farming (NCONF), Ghaziabad
content: Organic agriculture avoids synthetic inputs and enhances biological cycles, soil health, and biodiversity. Jeevamrit preparation: Mix 10 kg fresh indigenous cow dung, 10 litres cow urine, 2 kg jaggery, 2 kg pulse flour (besan), and a handful of fertile farm soil in 200 litres water. Stir clockwise twice daily and ferment in shade for 48-72 hours. Apply 200 litres Jeevamrit per acre with irrigation water or spray 10% solution on crops every 15-21 days as microbial inoculant. Beejamrit (Seed coating): 5 kg cow dung, 5 litres urine, 50g lime, and virgin soil mixed in 20 litres water; dip seeds before sowing to protect against soil-borne pathogens. Neemastra (Sucking pests): 5 kg crushed neem leaves + 5 litres cow urine + 2 kg cow dung fermented in 100 litres water for 48 hours; strain and spray against whiteflies, aphids, jassids. Brahmastra (Chewing caterpillars): Boil neem, custard apple, papaya, pomegranate, and guava leaves in cow urine; spray 2-3% solution. Certification: Farmers must register under Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) or Participatory Guarantee System of India (PGS-India) for verified organic certification.
